statement: A `'use client'` component must NEVER import, as a VALUE, a function from a shared/reused compose module (a script, service, or fixture file) that also carries server-only sibling imports at module scope (a Supabase admin client, a service that transitively reaches `node:crypto`/`node:fs`, etc.) — even when the specific function the client component calls is itself pure. A module's top-level imports are bundled as a unit regardless of which single export a caller uses; TypeScript's type system and a Vitest/Node test suite cannot detect this, because both resolve the import successfully in a Node environment where those server-only modules are perfectly loadable. The correct pattern is: compute the data in a Server Component (or another server-only context — a route handler, a server action), and pass the RESULT to the client component as a plain, already-computed prop. A client component may still import TYPES from such a module (`import type { ... }`) freely — type-only imports are erased at compile time and never reach the bundle — but never a runtime value.
classification: A Next.js App Router client/server module-boundary discipline, discovered as a specific instance of a broader gap: this repo's existing test suites (Vitest/tsc) structurally cannot verify client-bundle safety, because both execute in Node where every server-only module resolves fine. Only an actual `next build` (webpack) surfaces this class of defect. This candidate is the naming/documentation half of the lesson; the canary note below records that no automated enforcement exists yet for it in this repo.

canaries.assertion: Running `rm -rf .next && npm run build` on a branch that reintroduces this defect class reproduces a webpack `UnhandledSchemeError` (for `node:crypto` or an equivalent Node-only module) naming the offending client component in its import trace. No Vitest test or `tsc --noEmit` run can substitute for this — both were run for build-order item 11 and both passed despite the real defect being present.

occurrences.defect: UseCaseZeroDemoFixtureViewer.tsx ('use client') imported buildUseCaseZeroDemoFixture as a value from useCaseZeroDemoFixture.ts, which imports composeUseCaseZeroDemoChain as a value from scripts/seedUseCaseZeroDemo.ts — a file that ALSO carries server-only imports (getSupabaseServer, composeUnderwritingAdmissionEvidence, which itself transitively reaches services/identity/walletAliasService.ts's use of node:crypto) at module scope, by design, alongside its pure exports. next build failed with UnhandledSchemeError: node:crypto. 245 passing Vitest tests and a clean tsc --noEmit run had already been reported as this build item's verification, and neither caught it.

notes: This is the FIRST recorded occurrence — status stays `candidate`; only an operator act may raise this to `ratified`/`canonical`.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP, not implemented in this pass (deliberately out of this fix's scope per CLAUDE.md's Change Sizing rule): add a lightweight CI/local check that runs `next build` (or at least a webpack bundle-analysis pass) whenever a new client component is added under a directory that also contains server-only compose modules — Vitest and tsc alone are structurally insufficient. A cheaper interim option worth considering: apply the literal `server-only` npm package (already a dependency in this codebase, though currently only referenced in prose comments, not actually imported anywhere grepped) to files like scripts/seedUseCaseZeroDemo.ts so a future accidental client import fails LOUDLY with a clear message at build time, instead of an opaque webpack UnhandledSchemeError trace that has to be manually traced back to its root cause the way this occurrence required.

The natural second occurrence to watch for is any FUTURE dev-only fixture/demo/QA route (or any new client-rendered surface) that reuses a pure compose function from an existing script/service module for the same 'never hand-type a second copy' reason build-order item 11 itself cited (inv.engineering.036/037) — check whether that module's OTHER top-level imports are server-only before wiring a client component to call it directly.
